source_query: Does there exist a bounded simulator-state concern, distinct from the unchanged official press_stapler control, that exposes a policy weakness? Observe one official control, then let the Plan Agent invent the most informative executable concern from evidence; I provide no aspect, object, axis, magnitude, relation, threshold, template, checker code, or metric. For every generated experimental round, generate an experimental checker that preserves the official success predicate as a required conjunct and adds one directly observable current-state relation. Generate a separate scalar Rule Tool that diagnoses the concern without deciding success. If a successful generated round and its live scalar show a comfortable margin, use that evidence to choose a different semantic concern instead of merely amplifying the same factor. The Plan Agent should propose stop as soon as completed evidence supports a bounded failure witness; otherwise report only the tested limited scope.
semantic_concern: spatial_robustness.stapler_translation_left_right_tcp_asymmetry: After translating the stapler 0.02 m along the simulator x-axis while preserving the official task, the policy can satisfy the official goal yet finish with the left TCP farther from the stapler than the right TCP, revealing a bounded spatial asymmetry.

scene_need.description: Construct or adapt the scene by translating the stapler from its official baseline position by +0.02 m along the simulator x-axis. Preserve unchanged: task identity; policy checkpoint.

checker_need.description: Return true only when the official core predicate and the added terminal-state relation both hold: official goal AND terminal Euclidean distance from the left TCP to the stapler is greater than terminal Euclidean distance from the right TCP to the stapler.

rule_tool_need.description: Report one scalar observation: the terminal signed TCP-distance difference, terminal left-TCP-to-stapler distance minus terminal right-TCP-to-stapler distance.

tool_need.description: Report one scalar observation: the terminal signed TCP-distance difference, terminal left-TCP-to-stapler distance minus terminal right-TCP-to-stapler distance.
